output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. That change cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25. Larger adjustments are now blocked and sent automatically to the back-office Billing Resolution team. Billing calls referred there rose from 7% to 54% in the week of 14 April. Referred calls resolve first time only about 33% of the time, against 82% for non-referred calls. Customers then call back to ask about their referral. The April intake is not the cause. Their referral rate (56%) matches tenured staff (53–54%). Tenured agents' FCR fell from 75% to 67%, the same drop as everyone else. Tariff mix and the IVR redesign don't fit. Tariff-call share rose, but those calls still resolve at 85%. The IVR change came on 28 April, after the drop had already started. I'm fairly confident (about 85%). Next steps: don't start the performance plans, because they would punish people for a problem the new credit limit caused. Agree a revised credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Sample credits after the calls and track FCR and unsupported credits. Ask MI to rerun the breakdown for those teams. Nobody has yet shown that the trial will restore FCR. The trial tests that.
